reason: The development environment supplies signals that direct the stem-cell population toward connective-tissue work.
expectation: The signals will guide some cells toward a fibroblast identity.

effect: The signals directed a subset toward fibroblasts and activated a collagen gene, producing messenger RNA for ribosomes.
reaction: The connection from an external signal to gene activity is useful; the mesoderm precursor is not explained.
reason: The collagen messenger RNA can guide ribosomes in joining amino acids into a protein.

choice.combine: Developing fibroblasts with collagen messenger RNA

expectation: The fibroblasts will use the amino acids to make a collagen precursor.

effect: The fibroblasts have translated the collagen message into procollagen in the ER and Golgi; the next goal is to build extracellular material.
reaction: The RNA-to-protein connection is clear, though procollagen is not explicitly defined as a collagen precursor.
reason: The vesicles are shown carrying procollagen from the Golgi and fusing with the membrane, suggesting the next step is secretion.
expectation: The fibroblasts will release procollagen outside the cells.

effect: The vesicles released procollagen outside the fibroblasts, making it available for extracellular processing.
reaction: The secretion sequence connects the cell's protein production to its surroundings clearly.
reason: The enzyme picture shows procollagen being clipped and collagen molecules cross-linked outside the cell.
expectation: The enzymes will process the procollagen into cross-linked collagen.

effect: Extracellular processing produced cross-linked collagen fibers that resist tension.
reaction: The opposing arrows make the fibers' mechanical role clear.
reason: The hydrated proteoglycans are shown forming a gel around cells and collagen fibers, suggesting they complete the extracellular material.
expectation: The fibers and hydrated gel will form extracellular connective-tissue material.

effect: The collagen fibers and hydrated gel formed an extracellular matrix, completing the chapter; the fibroblasts remain distinct from the material they make.
reaction: The cell-versus-matrix inset is a useful clarification.

mostWorthwhile.text: Following the signal from gene activation through RNA and protein production to secretion connected familiar cell biology to the material surrounding cells.

leastWorthwhile.text: The mesoderm precursor appeared in the developmental sequence without explanation, making that transition harder to interpret.

surprise.text: The final illustration plan clarified that fibroblasts sit beside the matrix rather than becoming it.

arbitrary.text: Adding hydrated proteoglycans followed the picture, but their origin and specific contribution beyond forming a water-rich gel were not clearly explained.

continue.text: I would continue to see how extracellular material contributes to tissue function; the sequence made a useful connection between molecular processes and structure.
